title: All K-Picks From 1 to N
statement:
Given n and k, return every way to choose k different numbers from 1 to n. Order inside a choice does not matter, so [1, 3] and [3, 1] are the same choice and must appear only once.

Write each choice as a list in increasing order. The choices themselves may be returned in any order.

examples.why: Six pairs. [2, 1] is not listed again because it is the same pick as [1, 2].
Taking all three numbers can be done in exactly one way.
Each single number is its own pick.

gen: (r, big) => { if (big) return [18, 9]; const n = r.int(1, 8); return [n, r.int(1, n)]; }
hints: Build a pick one number at a time. To avoid listing the same set twice, what rule can you put on the next number you add?
Only add numbers larger than the last one you added. Then every set is built in exactly one way: in increasing order.
Prune: if you still need m more numbers and the next candidate is start, you need start + m − 1 ≤ n. Stop the loop early otherwise.

explain.intuition:
Each set of k numbers has exactly one increasing order. So if you only ever extend a partial pick with a number larger than its last element, every set is produced once and never as a reordering of another. That turns into a small recursion: choose the next number from start to n, recurse with start = chosen + 1, then undo the choice.

Pruning makes it tight: when m numbers are still missing, the next one cannot exceed n − m + 1, or there would not be enough larger numbers left to finish.
steps: Keep a list path for the current partial pick and a list out for finished picks.
go(start): if path has k numbers, push a copy to out and return.
Otherwise, with need = k − path.length, try each v from start to n − need + 1: push v, call go(v + 1), pop v.
pitfalls: Pushing path itself instead of a copy. Every saved pick then changes as the search goes on and ends up empty.
Restarting each level at 1 instead of at last + 1. That produces every ordering and repeats numbers.

solutions.title: Check every subset bitmask
solutions.idea: Every subset of 1..n is a bitmask from 0 to 2ⁿ − 1. Keep the masks with exactly k bits set and turn each into its list of numbers.

solutions.title: Backtracking in increasing order
solutions.idea: Extend the pick only with larger numbers, and stop early when there are not enough numbers left to finish it.

followups: Return only the m-th pick in increasing lexicographic order, without generating the ones before it.
Generate the picks so that consecutive picks differ by swapping just one number in and one out.
